title: I had Claude Code build me a 3D Formula1 racing game, complete with multiple classes, career mode, and realtime multiplayer.
author: ledniv

comments.author: MakanLagiDud3
comments.body: How? Would it be alright to share a tutorial?

replies.author: ledniv
replies.body:
First, I had already asked a separate Claude instance for the platform play.nitzan.games, so I had that up along with Node JS multiplayer. 

Then I asked a new Claude instance to create a 3d racing game. I said I wanted to keep it simple. We could use 2d physics and keep the track flat. I said I wanted to the track generation to be tile based, with straights, 2x2 curves and 3x3 curves. 

I explained that I want a start/finish line and the races will be 3 laps. 

I also explained grid spots and how cars should line up there. Claude suggested the player should always start from the back spot and I agreed.

Claude suggested how the AI should work and I agree to try it. It worked very well (even though I did not 100% understand it.)

It actually build the entire game at that point. I used the superpowers skills, so it asked a few questions, but it got to something very similar to what we have here very quickly. The cars were terrible though, the steering was flipped, and the track walls had issues.

Then I decided it should be an F1 game, so I asked it to give me a mockup of 4 F1 cars to choose from. I picked one, we iterated on it a bit until it looked good enough.

Then I explained I want it to have 20 tracks. With Claude's help we decided how many turns each track should have (start with 6, the last few have 20)

I said I want 4 classes, F4, F3, F2 and F1 and they should have different speeds. Claude decided on the speeds and it worked well. 

I also explained the controls. That it should be one touch, drag to steer, and the more you steer the slower the car goes. 

Also for all the trees and stuff I asked for mockups and then picked the best ones. Claude suggested to have one type of tree for each track to make them feel different.

That's about it. The whole thing took about 2 days.

replies.author: Ferreteria

replies.author: ledniv
replies.body:
I just told it what was wrong. Like: 

The front wing is too far forward of the front wheels. 

The nose is too pointy and needs to stop in the middle of the front wing. 

The rear wing is floating, add a polygon to connect it to the body. 

Add axels to the wheels so they are connected to the body.

comments.author: metsudo
comments.body: Impressive. Can you elaborate on how you got Claude to do the 3D models ? I didn’t think it could even generate images natively so imagine you must be using it to control Blender or something ? Can you share how ?

replies.author: ledniv
replies.body:
Claude can generate art and meshes, at least in Javascript/HTML5. You just need to ask it. It can also use python and math to generate the same images as pngs for Unity.

It can generate low-poly 3d models pretty well too.

What would be great is if Claude could talk to 3rd party services like Meshy, but I couldn't get that to work. 

Also it can generate sound effects and music using math. But it sounds a lot like PC sounds from the 90s.
